threat_event: Business email compromise: an adversary-in-the-middle phishing page steals a partner or tax manager session token, and the attacker harvests client documents from the mailbox and shared files
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Number matching MFA does not stop token theft; no device-compliance check for mail access; inbox-rule alerts suppressed in filing season; clients email source documents
existing_controls: MFA with number matching; legacy authentication and external forwarding blocked; email security gateway; quarterly phishing simulations
treatment_plan: Phishing-resistant security keys for partners, administrators, finance, and CAS payroll staff; require compliant devices for mail; restore inbox-rule alerts with tuning; token-theft detection rules (see P08 BEC runbook)
exposure_estimate_usd: $400K-$1.5M (response, notification of up to several thousand clients, refund fraud reimbursement)

threat_event: Attacker in a hijacked client or staff email thread asks the Company to change the refund direct deposit account on a return
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Call-back rule exists in the tax practice but is not enforced in the tax software workflow; seasonal staff not trained on it
existing_controls: Written call-back rule in the tax practice manual; reviewer check of bank changes
treatment_plan: Tax software workflow flag that blocks e-file release after a bank change until a call-back is logged; seasonal training before access

threat_event: Stolen client data or a compromised EFIN is used to file fraudulent returns in clients' names
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Data theft could go unnoticed in the tax software (no log collection); weekly EFIN and PTIN checks only in filing season
existing_controls: Weekly EFIN and PTIN returns-filed checks in season for all 6 EFINs
treatment_plan: Year-round monthly EFIN checks; tax software activity in the SIEM (R-030); data theft procedure with the IRS Stakeholder Liaison (P08)

threat_event: Ransomware with data theft (double extortion) encrypts the DMS, workpaper server, virtual desktops, and endpoints during filing season
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 14 standing administrator accounts on daily accounts; 9 non-expiring service accounts; untested restore of the workpaper server; no SaaS activity monitoring
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-03; SYS-04; SYS-11; BP-01 to BP-06
existing_controls: EDR with 24x7 MSSP; immutable backups in a separate account; DMS restore tested 2025; MFA for all staff
treatment_plan: Privileged access management for directory and SaaS administrators; vault and rotate service accounts; quarterly restore tests of DMS and workpaper server; ransomware runbook and executive tabletop (P08)
exposure_estimate_usd: $1.5M-$5M (outage in season, response, notification; insurance limit $15M)

threat_event: Bulk export of client files from the DMS or tax software by an attacker using a valid account, for extortion or resale
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No DMS or tax software logs in the SIEM; no egress volume alerting from the DMS subnet; all tax staff can open every tax client folder
existing_controls: EDR; SIEM on identity, email, and firewall; MFA
treatment_plan: Onboard DMS and tax software activity to the SIEM with bulk-download alerts; egress alerting; team-based DMS permissions
exposure_estimate_usd: $2M-$6M (up to 205,000 consumers notified; FTC notice; counsel, forensics, credit monitoring)

threat_event: Credential-stuffing campaign takes over client portal accounts and downloads returns or changes contact details
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Client MFA optional (58% enrolled); portal enrollment verifies email only
existing_controls: Vendor lockout and bot detection; TLS
treatment_plan: Mandatory client MFA before the 2027 filing season; identity check on portal enrollment; alert on contact detail changes

threat_event: Privileged account takeover: an attacker phishes an IT administrator's daily account with standing directory or productivity suite rights and changes MFA and conditional access
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 14 IT staff with standing administrator rights on daily accounts; no break-glass accounts for the identity provider or productivity suite; no phishing-resistant MFA
existing_controls: MFA with number matching; privileged access broker for cloud only
treatment_plan: Separate privileged accounts with security keys; just-in-time elevation for directory and SaaS administration; 2 break-glass accounts per critical tenant, tested quarterly

threat_event: A service account with directory administrator rights and a non-expiring password is used for lateral movement
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 9 service accounts with non-expiring passwords and broad rights
existing_controls: EDR; SIEM alerts on interactive sign-in by service accounts
treatment_plan: Vault and rotate service account credentials; reduce rights; managed service accounts where supported

threat_event: A seasonal staff member or intern keeps access after the season and views or copies client files
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Seasonal accounts disabled an average of 3 business days late; DMS rights from prior teams retained
existing_controls: End dates set at account creation; identity provider disables on the end date
treatment_plan: Automated disable on the HR end date; quarterly access reviews; transfer workflow removes prior DMS rights

threat_event: An employee copies client files to personal storage before leaving for a competitor
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No data loss prevention on uploads to personal cloud storage; DMS access not monitored
existing_controls: Confidentiality agreement citing IRC 7216; USB storage blocked
treatment_plan: Block uploads to unapproved cloud storage; DMS activity alerts; exit interview checklist

threat_event: Offshore vendor staff view SSNs of Form 1040 filers in scanned source documents, a disclosure 26 CFR 301.7216-3(b)(4) does not permit without the IRS-defined safeguards
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: SSN masking applies in the tax software but not to DMS images; consent capture not enforced before routing a return offshore (4 of 25 sampled lacked consent)
affected_asset_or_process: BP-06; SYS-03; SYS-04 virtual desktop pool
existing_controls: SSN masked in the tax software offshore role; U.S.-hosted desktops; no export or print
treatment_plan: Offshore-only DMS view of masked images; route returns offshore only after the consent is signed (portal workflow gate); counsel review of the IRS adequate-safeguard guidance before any unmasked use
exposure_estimate_usd: $100K-$1M (criminal and civil exposure under 26 U.S.C. 7216 and 6713, client remediation)

threat_event: Offshore vendor staff misuse or photograph client data on the virtual desktops
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No right-to-audit exercised; vendor staff turnover not reported to the Company
existing_controls: Desktops block export, print, and clipboard; vendor background checks per contract
treatment_plan: Annual vendor assessment with a site review; turnover reporting within 1 business day; session recording for the offshore pool

threat_event: A service provider with customer information is breached, and its contract has no security, notice, or audit terms
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 31 of about 85 service providers have no security terms; reviews only at onboarding
existing_controls: SOC 2 reviews for the tax software, portal, and cloud providers
treatment_plan: Vendor tiering under STD-03; contract amendments for all Tier 1 and Tier 2 providers; annual Tier 1 reviews (P09)

threat_event: A software vendor's own remote support tool, or the MSSP's access, is used as an entry point
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Two software vendors connect with their own remote tools without per-session approval; MSSP holds EDR response rights on every endpoint
existing_controls: MSSP SOC 2 Type 2; MSSP contract with security terms
treatment_plan: Route vendor support through the privileged access broker with session approval and recording; annual MSSP review

threat_event: Client data placed in unapproved SaaS tools (file sharing, e-signature, survey) is exposed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 41 unapproved SaaS applications found, 6 holding client data; no SaaS approval gate in purchasing for card spend
existing_controls: SaaS discovery tool; POL-05 approved-tools rule
treatment_plan: Block unapproved file sharing; migrate the 6 data-holding apps; card-spend review for SaaS

threat_event: Over-retention: files of about 95,000 former-client consumers kept past the retention schedule enlarge any breach
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 2024 retention schedule never executed in the DMS
existing_controls: Retention schedule adopted 2024
treatment_plan: First disposal run of files past the schedule with legal hold checks; annual run thereafter
exposure_estimate_usd: Adds about 46% to the notification population of a full DMS breach

threat_event: Tax software vendor outage or degradation in the last days before a filing deadline
threat_source: Vendor infrastructure failure or attack on the vendor
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Vendor RTO 8 h equals the BIA RTO; no deadline-week outage procedure; single tax platform
existing_controls: Vendor SOC 2 Availability criteria; remote work possible from any office
treatment_plan: Deadline-week vendor outage procedure (P08 variant); early-extension trigger rules; contract service credits and status commitments

threat_event: Recovery fails or takes longer than the RTO for the workpaper application or the CAS repeat-payroll fallback
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Workpaper server never restored; CAS fallback never exercised
existing_controls: DMS restore tested 2025; immutable backups
treatment_plan: Restore test of the workpaper server (2026-11-17); CAS repeat-payroll exercise with the vendor; annual recovery exercise calendar

threat_event: CAS payroll misses a client pay date because of a vendor outage or loss of Company identity services
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Payroll depends on the vendor and on staff reaching it through SSO; no exercised fallback
existing_controls: Payroll vendor SOC 2 RTO 4 h; vendor emergency processing line
treatment_plan: Documented repeat-payroll fallback; quarterly exercise; client communication templates

threat_event: Fraudulent request (email or phone) changes a vendor or employee bank account in a CAS client's bill pay or payroll, diverting client funds
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Bank changes in bill pay need one CAS approver; call-back not required for payroll direct deposit changes
existing_controls: Second approver for payment batches
treatment_plan: Call-back verification on a known number for every bank change; second approver for bank changes; 10-day hold on first payments to a changed account
exposure_estimate_usd: $100K-$2M per event (client funds lost, CAS client claims)

threat_event: CFO or vendor impersonation leads the Company's own accounts payable to pay a fraudulent bank account
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Call-back rule exists but is not documented for urgent wires
existing_controls: Dual approval for payments over $25,000
treatment_plan: Documented call-back for every bank change and every urgent wire request

threat_event: PHI from health care engagements, kept in the general DMS and workpaper folders, is exposed in a broader breach or viewed by staff without a need to know
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: PHI not segregated; no HIPAA risk analysis of the ePHI; BAAs require reporting of security incidents
existing_controls: BAAs for all 44 health care clients; DMS encrypted at rest
treatment_plan: Move PHI to the restricted enclave; HIPAA risk analysis for the ePHI; restrict access to engagement teams
owner: Attest Firm Quality and Independence Partner

threat_event: A notification deadline is missed (IRS next business day, FTC 30 days, Florida 30 days, other states, business associate notice) because discovery and determination dates are not recorded
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Discovery recording added in 2026 policy; untested; 4 of 15 staff unaware of the reporting channel
existing_controls: Notification matrix (P08); outside counsel through the insurer
treatment_plan: Decision log with discovery, confirmation, and determination dates; tabletop with counsel; reporting channel in training

threat_event: Returns and source documents sent as plain email attachments are intercepted or forwarded beyond the client
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Staff email returns on request (31 of 60 sampled were unencrypted)
existing_controls: Portal available for every client; TLS between mail servers where supported
treatment_plan: Data loss prevention rule that forces encryption or blocks tax attachments; portal-only delivery standard

threat_event: A return or source document is sent to the wrong client through email or the portal
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: High volume in season; manual addressing
existing_controls: Portal delivery ties documents to the client account
treatment_plan: Recipient warning for external addresses; incident procedure for misdirected documents

threat_event: A laptop or phone with cached client files is lost or stolen
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Staff travel to client sites in season
existing_controls: Full-disk encryption; MDM remote wipe
treatment_plan: Accepted: encryption makes the data unreadable (not an FTC notification event if keys are not compromised)

threat_event: Images stored on multifunction printer drives are recovered after the lease ends
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 8 older printers have unencrypted drives; no wipe certificate process at lease return
existing_controls: Newer printers encrypt drives
treatment_plan: Wipe certificate required at lease return; replace the 8 printers at renewal

threat_event: An internet-facing gateway (VPN or virtual desktop) is exploited through an unpatched flaw
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 6 of 40 sampled critical findings patched late; gateways patched monthly
existing_controls: Annual penetration test; monthly scans of internet-facing services; managed gateway services
treatment_plan: Known-exploited vulnerability patching within 7 days for internet-facing services; include the virtual desktop gateway in the 2026-11 penetration test

threat_event: A SaaS configuration change made outside change control weakens security or creates an unreviewed data flow (for example, enabling an AI feature)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: SaaS tenant changes by practice administrators bypass change control (AI drafting enabled 2026-03)
existing_controls: Infrastructure change board
treatment_plan: SaaS baselines in STD-01; change control for tenant settings; weekly configuration drift report from the SaaS posture tool

threat_event: An authorized user misuses the tax software (bulk export, browsing records of celebrities or relatives) without detection
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Tax software activity logs kept 90 days by the vendor and never reviewed
existing_controls: Role-based access in the tax software
treatment_plan: Collect tax software activity in the SIEM; monthly review of high-risk access; one-year retention

threat_event: Phishing during filing season captures credentials of seasonal staff who started before training
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 18% of seasonal staff got access before training; seasonal phishing waves start in January
existing_controls: Annual training; MFA
treatment_plan: No access until training is complete (identity provider group gate); January phishing simulation for seasonal staff

threat_event: AI document extraction (AI-001) places a wrong value on a return that the reviewer does not catch
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Accuracy lower on photographed and handwritten documents; reviewers trust AI-populated fields
existing_controls: Preparer verification of low-confidence fields; reviewer sign-off
treatment_plan: Mandatory verification of critical fields and photographed documents; monthly accuracy sampling (P10)

threat_event: The tax software AI drafting feature sends tax return information for substantive determinations without a confirmed IRC 7216 basis
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Feature enabled by the tax practice in 2026-03 without review; used on about 2,100 returns
existing_controls: Vendor terms state U.S. processing and no training
treatment_plan: Feature turned off 2026-08-28 pending counsel review; change control for AI features (P10)

threat_event: Staff paste client data into public generative AI chatbots
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: SaaS discovery found client names and notice text in public chatbot use by 9 staff; no block
existing_controls: POL-05 approved-tools rule; enterprise AI assistant available
treatment_plan: Block public chatbots on Company devices and networks; training on IRC 7216 and AI; sanctions applied in 3 cases

threat_event: AI resume screening (AI-005) ranks applicants in a way that has adverse impact on a protected group, or is used without the notices Colorado law requires from 2027-01-01
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Vendor model not validated locally; 2026 cycle selection-rate ratios for two race or ethnic groups below four-fifths, and age 40 and over far below; recruiters advance only top-ranked applicants
existing_controls: Recruiters can view all applicants
treatment_plan: Suspend auto-ranking for advance decisions; adverse impact testing each cycle; notice and human review process before Colorado-resident decisions on or after 2027-01-01 (P10)

threat_event: The AI tax research assistant (AI-003) cites a wrong or nonexistent authority that reaches a client memo or IRS response
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No mandatory citation check before 2026-09
existing_controls: Reviewer sign-off on client memos
treatment_plan: Mandatory citation check against primary sources; no client identifiers in prompts

threat_event: The journal entry analytics tool (AI-004) changes its model and misses unusual entries the audit team relies on
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Vendor release notes reviewed informally
existing_controls: Auditors design other procedures; partner review
treatment_plan: Change notice clause; validation on a reference data set before each new model version
owner: Attest Firm Quality and Independence Partner

threat_event: Contractor staff see tax return information without the written IRC 6713 and 7216 notice
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No written notice given to MSSP analysts, scanner maintenance technicians, or offshore vendor staff
existing_controls: Contracts include confidentiality terms
treatment_plan: Written notice to each contractor individual before access; annual re-acknowledgment

threat_event: A third-party disclosure (lender, adviser, offshore) is made before the IRC 7216 consent is signed, or after it expires
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Consent tracked in the portal, but release is not blocked; consents without a stated duration expire after one year (301.7216-3(b)(5))
existing_controls: Consent templates reviewed by counsel in 2024
treatment_plan: Portal workflow blocks release without a current signed consent; consent expiry report

threat_event: Configuration drift on cloud servers leaves logging or services in an insecure state
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No configuration standard; 31 deviations on 12 sampled servers
existing_controls: Guardrails; benchmark images
treatment_plan: Issue STD-01; monthly drift report; fix the 31 deviations

threat_event: A cloud storage bucket is exposed publicly
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Guardrails block public access in all accounts
existing_controls: Organization guardrails; posture alerts
treatment_plan: Quarterly guardrail review

threat_event: Internet or SD-WAN outage at the document processing center in peak season
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Dual ISP at Office 1; single ISP with untested cellular failover at 3 offices
existing_controls: Dual ISP at Office 1; staff can work remotely
treatment_plan: Test cellular failover at all offices before 2027 season

threat_event: Physical theft of paper source documents or devices from an office
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Network closets at Offices 4 and 6 use keys without a log; open print trays at Offices 4-6
existing_controls: Badge access; visitor logs; shredding
treatment_plan: Badge readers on the 2 closets; pull printing at Offices 4-6

threat_event: Key-person dependency: the small security team cannot cover incidents and projects in filing season
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Security team of 4; Director of Information Security is both Qualified Individual and operations lead
existing_controls: MSSP 24x7; insurer panel
treatment_plan: Add 1 security engineer (FY2027 budget); documented deputy for the Qualified Individual; MSSP surge hours in season

threat_event: The board receives an incomplete annual report and cannot oversee the program as 314.4(i) intends
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 2025 report omitted service providers and test results
existing_controls: Quarterly audit committee reporting started 2026
treatment_plan: 2026-10-27 written report covering every 314.4(i)(1)-(2) topic

threat_event: A planned acquisition of another CPA firm brings unassessed systems, accounts, and client data into the Company
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No security due diligence step in the acquisition playbook; the sponsor plans 2 acquisitions in 2027
existing_controls: IT integration checklist (technical only)
treatment_plan: Security due diligence and a 90-day integration plan for every acquisition; risk assessment update after each close

threat_event: An attacker or insider alters return data (refund amount or bank account) between review and e-file
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Review sign-off does not lock bank fields; e-file release allowed after later edits
existing_controls: Reviewer sign-off; separate e-file release role
treatment_plan: Tax software rule that requires re-review after any change to bank fields after sign-off

threat_event: SOC engagement evidence (client system descriptions, vulnerability results) leaks from the workpaper application
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Workpaper folders open to all assurance staff; SOC evidence includes client weaknesses
existing_controls: Workpaper application roles by engagement
treatment_plan: Engagement-level access for SOC files; quarterly review by engagement partners

threat_event: Identity provider outage stops access to every SaaS service
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single identity provider; no break-glass accounts for the productivity suite
existing_controls: Vendor SOC 2 Availability criteria
treatment_plan: Break-glass accounts for critical tenants (with R-007); outage procedure in P08

threat_event: An attacker impersonates an employee on a call to the service desk and gets an MFA reset
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Service desk verifies identity with employee ID and manager name, both easy to find
existing_controls: Callback to the number in the HR system for administrators only
treatment_plan: Video or in-person identity check, or manager approval in the identity provider, before any MFA reset

threat_event: Former CAS staff accounts in the payroll and bill-pay services (outside SSO) are used to change client payroll or payments
threat_source: Former staff; attacker using stale credentials
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Local accounts not tied to the HR leaver process; 3 former staff accounts found active in P07 (2026-08-14)
existing_controls: Accounts disabled 2026-08-14 after the finding
treatment_plan: Federate the payroll and bill-pay services to SSO with security keys; monthly reconciliation of local accounts until then

threat_event: Paper source documents and printed returns at remote workers' homes are not shredded
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 25% of staff work remotely; home printing allowed
existing_controls: POL-05 clean desk rule
treatment_plan: Disable home printing for client documents; shredding reimbursement where printing is approved
